title: STAT+: Why this startup is taking its AI to predict breast cancer risk directly to patients
source_used: Everyday Health (STAT+ page paywalled; only its opening and subhead readable)
key_facts: Clairity Breast, an FDA-authorized AI tool, estimates a woman's 5-year breast cancer risk from a recent screening mammogram.
It is now sold nationwide through digital health company Everlywell for $249, self-pay and not covered by insurance; before it was available only at select sites in Massachusetts and Colorado.
Buyers need a qualifying screening mammogram from the past 12 months; an Everlywell-network clinician reviews and orders it and shares results.
It currently works only with Hologic mammograms; it does not detect or diagnose cancer.
Everlywell's release was dated 1 Oct 2026 (Business Wire, per Everyday Health's sources).
An outside breast surgeon says a high-risk result means a 3% or greater five-year chance, still low in absolute terms, and that FDA authorization means safe, not proven to improve outcomes.
STAT's subhead: waiting on doctors and insurers to get on board would have taken too long, Clairity says.
quote_evidence: The $249 test assesses a woman’s risk of developing breast cancer over the next 5 years.
The FDA authorization means the tool is safe, not that it improves outcomes.
why_it_matters_hint: Direct-to-consumer AI risk score that insurance does not cover.
notes: STAT+ article is paywalled (only lede and subhead read); facts from Everyday Health, 6 Oct 2026. Launch before the window, so score lowered by 1.
